item.title: Show HN: Podframes - local pipeline for generating podcast videos (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: Hi HN, I built Podframes because the "speech to video" part of podcast generation kept turning into a pile of one-off scripts. The repo is a local pnpm project that takes a topic and produces a two-host podcast-style video. It writes a script, generates the conversation audio, keeps word-level timings, makes one video clip per spoken turn, then renders the final MP4 with captions. The main thing I wanted was not another black-box video generator. I wanted the intermediate files to be boring and inspectable. A run creates a project directory with the script, audio, timing data, stills, clips, composition files, captions, and final output. If a line changes, the goal is to rerun only the parts affected by that line instead of paying for the whole video again. It is not fully local or offline. You still need provider keys for the media models. The local web UI is also not meant to be deployed publicly. It is a studio for editing/rerunning a project on your own machine. The repo is here: https://github.com/Jellypod-Inc/podframes I would be especially interested in feedback on the architecture: whether the per-turn resume model makes sense, whether the project directory layout is understandable, and what would make this easier to try without hiding the fact that video generation costs money. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48777365 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
